facts.raw_span: A man in his 40s presented with a new pigmented lesion on his left second toenail
The lesion first appeared 12 months before presentation and was progressively growing
The lesion was asymptomatic
He was otherwise well and denied any fevers or weight loss
dark brown longitudinal pigment band covering the full length of the toenail of the left second digit with corresponding nail thickening over the pigmented band
The pigment was the same width throughout the band and extended to the proximal nail fold
No other nail or skin lesions were found at the time of examination
Bland spindle cell proliferation within the nail matrix with invaginations of the epithelium
No melanocytic lesions observed
Immunostaining negative for S100 and CD34
Intracorneal hemorrhage and adjacent verrucous hyperkeratosis present
Villous fibroepithelial projections into the nail plate without melanocytic proliferation or keratinocyte atypia

concepts.why: The presence of bland spindle cell proliferation within the nail matrix and villous fibroepithelial projections into the nail plate without melanocytic proliferation or keratinocyte atypia supports the diagnosis of onychopapilloma.
The presence of a dark brown longitudinal pigment band covering the full length of the toenail with corresponding nail thickening over the pigmented band is consistent with longitudinal melanonychia.
The presence of a pigmented lesion within the nail matrix and the absence of melanocytic lesions observed on histopathologic examination could suggest a nail matrix nevus.
The presence of nail thickening over the pigmented band is consistent with onychauxis.
The presence of intracorneal hemorrhage and adjacent verrucous hyperkeratosis supports the diagnosis of subungual keratosis.
The presence of nail thickening over the pigmented band could also suggest nail plate sclerosis.
The presence of a pigmented lesion and nail thickening could suggest onychodystrophy.
The presence of intracorneal hemorrhage supports the diagnosis of subungual hematoma.
The immunostaining negative for S100 and CD34, along with the bland spindle cell proliferation within the nail matrix, points towards onychomatricoma.
